cells.tense: You are tending something small right now, with your hands in it.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Ask of whatever you're growing whether it's finished or still going. When it's done, take your hands off it and leave the unfinished one your attention.
cells.core:
Nothing has chosen a direction yet where you're standing, and that's the ground you're working. You tend things and learn them by tending — how much water, how much light, when to step back and let a thing go its own way. That part is working. Your attention stays on what is actually growing rather than on what you'd like it to become, and something cared for that way comes out shaped like itself.
The invitation is to stop at the right moment. Somewhere near you is a thing you keep feeding past its finish — a task that's clean already, a habit that's served its turn. Let that one rest and move the hours onto what's still unfinished. When a completed thing is left alone, there is more space around what's left, and that space is easy to notice.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's growing and what's already finished.
cells.verb: tending something and learning from it how it grows
cells.place: the open space before anything has been chosen

cells.tense: You will have arranged everything ahead of the moment it arrives.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Leave a plan of yours alone for a few days. Picture the next step the way you'd like it to go, feel it out, then take a piece of it that same day.
cells.core:
You tend well, and lately the care has gone past what's here to tend. Things that haven't started get tended in advance — plans worked through three moves deep, worries solved before they arrive, ground prepared for seasons that may not come. That is a lot to carry. The preparedness is the tell: the future gets met with the shoulders already up.
What pulls this back is care that starts from what's on the table now. Go look at one of these pre-planned things before you've settled how it should go, and let what you find set the shape. Dream the next step from what's really there rather than from what you've prepared for, then take one small piece while the imagining is fresh. Carrying less leaves the hands free.

cells.tense: The moment to begin has passed, and you are still at that door.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin a page or a pot or a line of something for the pleasure of beginning, with no goal attached, and stop whenever the fun runs out.
cells.core:
Something has been waiting at the edge of starting and you haven't crossed over. Not from lack of ability — you know how to tend a thing, how to water and wait. But nothing has been put in the ground, and there is a quiet sense that this has gone on a while.
Starting is what refills this. Not the whole project, not a plan — the live act of setting something in motion because motion is the pleasure. Begin a thing with no future attached and give it a short run. Energy from a beginning travels a long way here and reaches the part of you parked at the edge. Once something is moving, caring for it follows easily, and the door is just where you happened to stand.
cells.sheetLine: You've been at the door a long time and haven't begun.

cells.tense: You're the one letting things grow here while calling it nothing.
cells.act: govern by knowing what to surrender
cells.ask: Find a duty you took on for someone that was handed to you by no one, and set it down this week — a task that would get done without you, a worry you picked up early.
cells.core:
Growth shows up around you because of something you keep doing — a plant gets watered, a date gets held, someone keeps showing up because you keep showing up. Ask you and it's just how things are. What you do doesn't get a name.
That isn't small, and it doesn't need a speech. What it needs is one place where you let go on purpose. Pick a thing you've been carrying that isn't yours to finish and set it down — a duty you took on before anyone asked, a task that would survive without you. What belongs to you stays. Releasing the rest leaves you lighter, and the growth around you stops feeling like something that just happened.
cells.sheetLine: The growth around you is your doing, and you'd say it just happened.

attempts.check: Two soft spots. First, Potential plus Bridge makes me reach for phrases like 'edge of something' — that's mine, not the record's, and a reader could fairly say they aren't aware of any door or threshold at all. Second, the Too Much core implies the person can see that plans are being laid in advance; if their own account is that they simply care a lot, my read overrules them. All four asks stand on their own if the read is wrong — each is a small thing done this week regardless of the diagnosis. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line about 'before it has a shape' in the Unacknowledged cell: it flatters the card's vocabulary, so I've cut it.
